body:
Founder real-time, mid-DEADWEIGHT-WS-bridge-debug: 'take the shankpit bot queue down to 8' then, after I reported it was already at 8 and flagged REDGARDEN as the bigger memory hog, clarified 'the shankpit bot pool goes down to 4'. Box was at 12.4Gi/15Gi used with swap 100% full, and iduna.service was actively OOM-killed and restart-looping (killed at 07:45:46, restarted, killed again at 07:46:18) as a direct result -- this was blocking the /api/ proxy WOTAN's DEADWEIGHT client depends on for SSO exchange. Edited both the live unit (~/.config/systemd/user/shankpit-bot-pool.service) and the repo copy (SHANKPIT/ops/systemd/shankpit-bot-pool.service), ExecStart bot_count 8->4, daemon-reload + restart. Verified: exactly 4 frozen_policy_bot.py processes running post-restart, free memory 352Mi->2.8Gi, swap used 495Mi(full)->266Mi, iduna.service stable (no further OOM-kills, 3+ min uptime) and https://wotan.okemily.com/api/v1/games/deadweight/decks back to real 200s. Commit SHANKPIT@492be5d.

⚓ ☃
title: Scale SHANKPIT queue bot pool 8->4 to relieve box-wide memory pressure
